pull.title: KAFKA-21341: Report a TLS close_notify without a TCP FIN as a disconnect
pull.body:
When a TLS `close_notify` arrives in the same read as application data,
`SslTransportLayer.read` returns the data and leaves the close for a
later read, but `updateBytesBuffered` clears `hasBytesBuffered`, so the
Selector never reads the channel again unless a TCP FIN arrives. A peer
may close only its TLS write side and keep the TCP connection open
(RFC 8446 section 6.1, e.g. a TLS-terminating proxy), and a request on
that connection then waits for `request.timeout.ms`.

The channel now stays in the buffered-read set after a `CLOSED` unwrap,
and the next read throws `EOFException` once the engine's inbound side
is done, so the disconnect is reported at once, as it already is when
`close_notify` arrives without data. A scattering read returns the
bytes it has already read instead of losing them to that exception.

Testing: new tests in `SslTransportLayerTest`, where a TLS peer sends a
partial or a full response plus `close_notify` in one write and keeps
the TCP connection open. The client must report the disconnect within
5 s (and deliver the full response), including when the channel is
muted after the response and later unmuted. The tests fail without the
fix.
